title: Record first decision-sets backtest and revise its design doc
summary: Design-only edit of docs/design/decision-sets.md: add a backtest-result section with real ids (D11/D39, D87, job 9h2j, 405), decide partial revisions, and add new signals and validation. Assumes partial revisions are 'amended_by', not 'superseded'.

defaults_applied.how: Backtest numbers and ids are cited from the user's run and the design's line references.
Section written so an outsider can follow the ids.
Design addresses the signal-vocabulary gap, not just the D87 instance.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Partial revisions are recorded as 'amended_by', since the original decision still stands in part.
The BRIEF.md addendum exists as quoted and can be cited.
Real ids come from the user's request; records/ is not readable here, so the producer must not invent other details.
Design only: no implementation of the host-error record or validation.

acceptance_criteria.text: The design has a backtest-result section stating the run failed, with the supersession parse (24 hits, 0 lacking a target, plus the unexpected D11 'Revised ... superseded by D39' at line 322) and the D87 signal finding (0 jobs for class docs, threshold 2).
The doc decides partial revisions: they are 'amended_by', not 'superseded', with the reason and how the expected list is corrected to include D11/D39.

The doc names the real interventions: job 20261013-192156-ar1x (9h2j), the hand squash of PR #41 after the HTTP 405, class code, the only one after D87; kn3q and qk2d predate it. D87's signal is revised to class code.
The doc specifies that a host error falsifying a decision's stated assumption puts it under review on first occurrence, while soft signals such as friction require repeats.
The doc specifies a host-error record (review F3) so the 405 is no longer only in intervention prose.
The doc requires signal field values to be validated against the record vocabulary so a signal cannot name an unrecorded class.

The doc adds a signal from the BRIEF.md addendum '2026-10-14: Common sense over rigid rules': a rule rejecting work that does not go against its stated intent is a failure signal for that rule, citing the addendum.
Only docs (and optionally CHANGELOG) change; no code, config, or records files are touched.

out_of_scope: Implementing the host-error record, signal validation, or new signals in code
Changing the backtest command or records
